handDesc.handNote: Main text and any darker interventions are distinguished where observed. No individual historical correcting hands are inferred from tonal contrast in monochrome photographs.

origin.p: The supplied BnF IIIF manifest dates the manuscript to 1001–1100. The catalogue dating is not a date assigned to individual interventions.

surrogates.p: The original full-resolution digital images and enlarged crops were inspected for this first pass. Gallica source reuse conditions apply. No text was populated from LL or another witness.

Émile Chatelain, Paléographie des classiques latins II, plate XCI notice1 (printed II,1; PDF fifth page): the direct manuscript description records Amores through3.12.26, resuming3.14.3, and blank paper marking a lacuna. This boundary evidence was independently checked alongside the photographs.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded audit of the photographed discontinuity between surviving text assigned to Amores 3.12 and the next surviving text, 3.14. No identifiable verse of 3.13 survives in this inspected sequence. A whole-poem gap records the 36 canonical alignment positions without supplying any wording. The source photographs and exact boundary have received an independent second review.

correction.p: No silent emendation from an edition or another witness. Local uncertain letters use unclear, irrecoverable text or signs use gap. Observed above-line letters use add. Tonal distinctions use hi without an invented underlying erased text or historical hand. Manuscript annotations use note type manuscript, distinct from editorial evidence notes.

normalization.p: One source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs, long s, and capitals are represented in legible Latin types. Word boundaries are editorially segmented; no indentation whitespace is inserted inside verse mixed content. Selected ligatures and abbreviation signs are declared typographic approximations; explicit expansions remain in TEI rather than a separate reading mode. This is not a facsimile-perfect inventory of every minute stroke.

punctuation.p: Significant observed punctuation is retained schematically, without adding systematic modern sentence punctuation.

segmentation.p: This absence record contains no verse transcription and no invented line rectangles. The whole-poem gap points to the two full source surfaces establishing the discontinuity. The quantity of 36 is the project canonical alignment extent, not an observed count of physically lost lines or a reconstructed number of original leaves. Blank inserted/support leaves are distinguished from obliterated surviving writing.

interpretation.p: Every source position and note has received an independent second reading. The companion ledger records resolved boundary evidence and documented image uncertainty; the latter is not a user task.

revisionDesc.change: Independent inspection of full images97–98, all continuous source strips and original annotation crops, and every evidence note. Verified the3.12.26 to3.14.3 discontinuity against Chatelain’s direct manuscript description. Retained source uncertainty and original coordinates; no text supplied from another witness.

Completed first-pass source-coverage audit of full images 97 and 98 and enlarged boundary crops. No surviving identifiable 3.13 text was found between the blackened 3.12 page and surviving 3.14. Independent verification pending.

gap.desc: No identifiable text of canonical Amores 3.13 is present in the inspected surviving sequence. Image 97 has a blackened page with the earlier 3.12 annotation sequence and an intervening blank leaf carrying Desunt hic quaedam; image 98 has the blank reverse and the next surviving text, 3.14. Thirty-six canonical positions are represented by this gap. Chatelain’s direct manuscript description corroborates the exact boundary3.12.26 to3.14.3. No missing wording, original leaf count, historical cause, or date of loss is inferred.

div.head: First-pass source-absence evidence
div.note: Independent inspection of full images 97 and 98 and continuous enlarged strips shows a blackened page carrying the surviving 3.12 region, an intervening blank support leaf with Desunt hic quaedam, and the next surviving verse text on image 98. Readable rows there include crimina pone tuo, identifying 3.14; the later Ex XIII. eleg. label does not override that identification. Chatelain’s manuscript description explicitly lists transmission through 3.12.26 and resumption at 3.14.3, independently supporting the exact canonical boundary. Neither the number of originally lost leaves nor a historical cause is inferred. This supports the absence of canonical3.13.1–36; missing annotations alone were not used as evidence.

The precise words beneath blackening at the end of image97 and top of98 remain unreadable. The external description corroborates the transmission boundary; it does not reveal those letters, reconstruct original P wording of3.13, or establish an original leaf count or historical cause.

The later label Ex XIII. eleg. is visible on image98. The readable verse sequence belongs to canonical3.14, and Chatelain specifies resumption at3.14.3. The label is old numbering, not surviving evidence for the missing canonical3.13.
